source: Empty pending a chart-specific source. Schema and rendering plumbing are in place (issue #399 / PR #401); data will be populated once a citable source — paragraph in PAMAT chapter B-03, an IAA AIP supplement that names the points, or direct visual inspection of the printed IAA CVFR chart — is available. Sources previously consulted (no extractable per-point comm-change data): Israel eAIP 2025-10-02 AIRAC AD 2.22 LLHA / LLBG / LLER, ENR 2.1, GEN 3.4, ENR 6-1 ATS routes chart; LLHZ / LLIB / LLOV AD 2 pages 404 in public eAIP; PAMAT (Israeli Domestic AIP) edition 1/24 (chart legend names the 'נקודת מעבר קשר' symbols but the symbol-to-waypoint mapping lives on graphical pages, not OCR-extractable). Last reviewed 2026-05-28.
_definition: Each entry marks a CVFR reporting point where pilots are expected to switch ATC frequencies because the point sits on (or at) a sector / CTR / TMA boundary. The chart annotation may be on the boundary line itself rather than directly at the point — the dataset records the *point of change*, not the chart-text position.
_NOTE: Reporting-type (חובה / דרישה — mandatory vs. on-request) is NOT comm-change. Sector-boundary proximity (a nav waypoint sitting geometrically close to a published PLUTO/HAGAV or TMA boundary line) is ALSO NOT a reliable proxy for comm-change. A point is a comm-change point only when a chart-specific source says so — a paragraph in PAMAT chapter B-03, an IAA AIP supplement naming the point, or direct inspection of the printed IAA CVFR chart symbology ('מע.' / 'מז.' / the 'נקודת מעבר קשר' legend symbols). Earlier inferences from boundary geometry (SORES, NSHRM, TZUBA, ZUKIM, BAZRA, HADRA, FRDIS, BOREN) and from sector-boundary chart text ('פלוטו מע.' near TYONA) were removed because they did not meet that bar; the chart-text annotation labels the boundary LINE, not the dot. Re-populate this file only with entries backed by a chart-specific citation in the per-entry `source` field.
_TODO: Source a chart-specific reference for each comm-change reporting point: ideally PAMAT chapter B-03 (Israeli Domestic AIP, CVFR section) which is graphical and requires page-by-page inspection, an IAA AIP supplement, or direct reading of the printed IAA CVFR chart legend ('נקודת מעבר קשר בנתיב' / 'נקודת מעבר קשר בין יחידות מבקרות בציון אות הקריאה').

Until a chart-specific source surfaces, leave `points: []` empty. The renderer (draw.js drawNavWaypoints, interact.js showInspector) tolerates the empty array — no rings drawn, no inspector badge — so the schema and infrastructure can merge ahead of the data.
Reporting-type data (mandatory / on-request) is tracked separately on the feat/reporting-required branch (PR #405) — DO NOT conflate the two datasets.
